binders: A real speed c, universally quantified; the assertion is conditional on c being strictly positive.
For the monotonicity clause, arbitrary real x, t1, and t2.
For the traveling-profile clause, an arbitrary profile f : Real -> Real, an arbitrary candidate derivative f' : Real, and arbitrary real x and t.
hypotheses: Within the monotonicity implication, t1 < t2.
Within the traveling-profile implication, f has derivative f' at x - c t.
conclusions: The 1 by 1 real matrix A_c = [c] admits a basis of real eigenvectors with associated real eigenvalues.
For every real x, t1, and t2, t1 < t2 implies x + c t1 < x + c t2.
For w(x,t) = f(x - c t), whenever f is differentiable at x - c t, there exist the time and space partial derivatives of w at (x,t), and they satisfy w_t(x,t) + c w_x(x,t) = 0.
The same traveling profile satisfies w(x + c t,t) = f(x).
mathematical_definitions: A_c is the 1 by 1 matrix with its only entry equal to c.
The matrix predicate means: there exist a real eigenvalue for each finite index and an indexed basis of the real coordinate space such that A_c b_p = lambda_p b_p for every index p.
w : Real x Real -> Real is defined by w(x,t) = f(x - c t).
The pointwise transport predicate means that witnesses q_t and q_x are derivatives of tau -> w(x,tau) at t and xi -> w(xi,t) at x, respectively, and q_t + c q_x = 0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every strictly positive real speed c, the scalar 1 by 1 coefficient matrix [c] has a complete real eigenbasis, and forward characteristic positions x + c t are strictly increasing in time. Moreover, for every real-valued profile f, derivative value f', and point (x,t), if f is differentiable with derivative f' at x - c t, then the traveling profile w(x,t) = f(x - c t) has both pointwise partial derivatives there and satisfies the constant-speed transport equation w_t + c w_x = 0; it also exactly recovers the profile along the characteristic shift, w(x + c t,t) = f(x).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is restricted to strictly positive speeds through the outer implication c > 0; it makes no assertion for c <= 0.

The coefficient condition concerns only a constant scalar 1 by 1 real matrix. In one dimension the existence of a real eigenbasis is essentially automatic and does not express a nontrivial multi-component hyperbolic system.

The transport statement is conditional and pointwise: for a given profile and point it has content only when the profile is differentiable at x - c t. It does not assume or conclude global differentiability.
The derivative value f' from the premise is not named in the conclusion; the partial derivative values are existential witnesses constrained only by their derivative predicates and the zero residual.
No initial-value problem, boundary condition, uniqueness theorem, regularity beyond the stated pointwise differentiability, or claim about all solutions of the transport equation is encoded.
The eigenbasis predicate requires a real basis and real eigenvalues but states no eigenvalue ordering, normalization, distinctness, or quantitative conditioning of the basis.
